features.name: Academic Preparation
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment the applicant cites.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic Systems Architecture
features.description: Captures hands-on design ownership of agent-based systems, especially their orchestration, boundaries, supervision, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI Production Maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has shipped AI or model-backed systems in production and understands reliability, evaluation, or guardrail concerns.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaborative Learning Mindset
features.description: Captures coachability, collaboration with security specialists, and attention to working with internal users rather than presenting the work as purely solo.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear collaboration or internal-customer orientation.
Uses generic team language, but without a concrete sense of collaborators or users.
Explicitly mentions partnering with security engineers or serving developer teams.
Clearly frames success as collaborative enablement, including learning from specialists and building thoughtfully for other engineers.

features.name: Developer Enablement Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames security tooling as helping engineers do the safe thing easily through defaults, usability, and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Distinctive Voice
features.description: Captures whether the letter feels memorable, individualized, and non-templated in its framing or prose voice.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Engineering Rigor
features.description: Captures emphasis on correctness, maintainability, failure awareness, testing, guardrails, and dependable long-term operation in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.name: Evidence Specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter substantiates claims with concrete mechanisms, examples, scope, outcomes, or impact rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go Backend Depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's production backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Narrative Coherence
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a clear, connected story or career arc rather than a disconnected list of claims.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures ongoing adversarial security practice outside ordinary development work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution, upstream repair, or maintainer responsibility in public codebases or software used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream fixes or small patches.
Shows regular contribution behavior, such as repeatedly patching dependencies or contributing upstream when issues are found.
Shows maintainer-level ownership with reviews, releases, community support, or a project used beyond the applicant's team.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, relevance, and seriousness of self-directed projects outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational or central tooling whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Python Engineering Depth
features.description: Captures how deeply and concretely the applicant shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Relevant Production Experience
features.description: Captures the depth, breadth, and maturity of the applicant's professional experience shipping, maintaining, testing, and owning production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Role-Specific Fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter connects the applicant's motivations and background to this exact role, team, or set of responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: States interest in the job with little or no explanation of why this team or mission is specifically appealing.
Shows generic interest in security or backend work but gives only broad reasons that could fit many roles.
Gives a clear role-specific reason such as foundational leverage, secure-by-default work, or security impact at scale.
Connects the role-specific reason to the applicant's own experience or values in a persuasive way.
Uses distinctive, well-developed framing that makes the applicant's motivation for this exact role feel unusually thoughtful and credible.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures the depth and concreteness of hands-on security review work such as threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, code review, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security Automation Framing
features.description: Captures whether the applicant understands the role as scaling scarce security judgment through tooling and automation rather than as generic software work.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security Credential Strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal external security credentials used to validate security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a foundational or introductory credential such as Security+ or an equivalent baseline certification.
Mentions a hands-on advanced credential such as OSCP or an equivalent practical certification.

features.name: Security Philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful point of view about what secure engineering work is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability Triage Automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building automation for vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, prioritization, or related workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures proofreading quality and sentence-level mechanical professionalism, including spelling, grammar, and typographical accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures genuinely idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly share an underlying construct with the recurring criteria above.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.
